finding: Possible side-channel smell: `settle` hands its two results (record, start flag) back through the closure dict `decided`, and `decided.clear()` is dead
why: safe_write.update_locked calls `transform` exactly once (scripts/safe_write.py:63-66), so the clear guards a re-run that never happens, and `chosen` is rebound from parsed marker to new record inside one 27-line closure, so readers must trace both writers of `decided` to know what `plan` gets back.
fix: Drop `decided.clear()`; have `settle` close over a small named result (or split into `recorded(text)` / `begin(...)`) so `chosen` and `start` are assigned in one place each.
evidence: `decided: dict = {}` ... `decided.clear()` ... `decided.update(chosen=chosen, start=True)` (x2) ... `chosen = fresh(root, name, pane, facts, marker)`

finding: A finished move whose worktree was later removed outside remove-worktree is restarted under the same name and fails forever
why: The restart branch keeps chosen['name'] even when the helper already recorded `created`, so create-worktree refuses it every RETRY_AFTER window ('branch ... already exists' / 'name ... already taken') and the session never gets a fresh worktree.
fix: In settle, when the marker holds `created` and its path is gone, fall through to fresh() with a new name; restart under the old name only when no `created` was recorded.
evidence: h2_move.py:135-141 `elif started recent: keep ... else: chosen.pop("error", None); decided.update(chosen=chosen, start=True); return json.dumps(dict(chosen, started=time.time()))`; scripts/afk-move.py:268 records `{"created": str(path)}`; scripts/create-worktree:596 `! git ... rev-parse --verify -q "refs/heads/$BRANCH" ... || error_exit "branch '$BRANCH' already exists; choose another name"`. Failing input: marker {name:session-ab12cd34, created:<path>}, user runs `git worktree remove <path>` (branch stays; remove-worktree.py drop_markers is not run), same session id refuses again after 180 s.

finding: New `settle` branches in h2_move.plan have no negative test: marker lacking `started`, valid JSON that is not a dict or has no `path`
why: `settle` (hooks/lib/h2_move.py:128-141) sends a marker with a non-numeric/missing `started` and a missing worktree straight to restart, and a path-less or non-dict marker to a fresh move; every marker written before this change has no `started`, and no test pins either outcome.
fix: Add tests for a marker without `started` (restarted, then stamped with `started`) and for `{}` / `[]` / `{"name":"x"}` markers (replaced by a fresh move).
evidence: hooks/lib/h2_move.py:128-135 `if isinstance(chosen, dict) and chosen.get("path"): started = chosen.get("started") ... elif isinstance(started, (int, float)) and time.time() - started < RETRY_AFTER`; the only restart test (test_a_stale_marker_..., line 746) always supplies a numeric old `started`

finding: Helper-does-not-start test cannot tell 'recorded, not retried' from 'retried and failed again'
why: the stubbed spawn raises the same OSError text on every call, so a second call that wrongly restarted the move would return an identical error and still pass `again["error"] == chosen["error"]`, and the test never counts spawn calls on the second plan().
fix: Collect spawn calls in the stub (append then raise) and assert exactly one call after the second plan(), or make the stub raise a different message the second time.
evidence: `def broken(argv, env): raise OSError("no such interpreter")` ... `again = module.plan(...)` / `assert again["error"] == chosen["error"]`

finding: Module docstring says one creation per session is keyed by the pane id, but plan() keys the marker by the session id and uses the pane only when no session id is present
why: The docstring was rewritten in this slice (lines 7-11 added) and still states the opposite of the key code at line 114, so a reader trusting it would expect a /cd (which changes the session id) to keep the marker.
fix: Reword to 'keyed by the session id, else by the pane id', matching line 114.
evidence: h2_move.py:5-6 'One creation per session, keyed by the pane id when there is one (the H-2 session id changes on `/cd`), else by the session id.' vs :114 'key = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]", "_", session or f"{pane}:nosession")'.

finding: Possible: marker docstring says every read and write runs under the lock, but remove-worktree.py reads and unlinks the same *.move markers with no lock
why: The round-8 fixes for f082, f071 and f061 removed an unlocked unlink of the current marker from plan(), and the same pattern still stands in the sibling consumer, so a marker can vanish or be replaced between plan()'s exists-check and read, or just after a restart rewrote it.
fix: Narrow the docstring to plan() and the helper, or make drop_markers re-read the marker and drop it only when the path it names is still the removed worktree's.
evidence: h2_move.py:9-10 'Every read and write of the marker runs under the safe writer's lock, so no call sees it half-written'; scripts/remove-worktree.py:253-255 'for marker in (common / "afk-session").glob("*.move"): ... json.loads(marker.read_text(...))', :262-264 'if same(target, path): marker.unlink(missing_ok=True)', :271 'marker.stat().st_mtime'. Pattern: enumerated every consumer of '*.move' / 'afk-session' (consumers checked: remove-worktree.py, protected_branch_guard.py:451-458, afk-move.py:119-138, worktree-prune.sh:11 which touches only *.fallback). Found by reading; not run.

finding: Possible mysterious names: `failed(...)` reads as a predicate but builds an error record; `fresh(...)` does not say it places a move or returns `failed()`
why: A caller must read the bodies to learn that `failed` returns a dict and that `fresh` may return an error result, which `settle` then probes with `.get("error")`.
fix: Rename to `error_move(...)` / `new_move(...)` (or inline `fresh`, which has one caller).
evidence: `def failed(name, pane, why) -> dict: ... return {"name": name, "path": "", "pane": pane, "error": why}`; `def fresh(root, name, pane, facts, marker) -> dict:`

finding: A marker written by earlier code (no `started`) whose path is not yet created is restarted at once instead of aged
why: The `isinstance(started, (int, float))` test fails for a marker without the field, so the else branch spawns a second helper for the same name while the first is still creating it, and the loser's `error` can land in the marker.
fix: When `started` is absent, age the marker by its file mtime (or stamp `started` and keep) rather than restarting.
evidence: h2_move.py:135-141 `elif isinstance(started, (int, float)) and time.time() - started < RETRY_AFTER: ... else: ... decided.update(chosen=chosen, start=True)`; the base marker shape was {name,path,pane,marker} (diff -2267 `chosen["marker"] = str(marker)`) with age read from mtime (diff -2284). No test in scripts/tests/test_h2_move.py writes a marker without `started`.

finding: Possible duplicated knowledge: the 'record a move as started and spawn it' tail appears twice in `settle`
why: Lines 139-141 (RETRY restart) and 146-147 (fresh move) each do `decided.update(chosen=chosen, start=True)` then `return json.dumps(dict(chosen, started=time.time()))`; a change to the start record must be made twice.
fix: Extract one `begin(chosen)` that sets `decided` and returns the stamped JSON, and call it from both branches.
evidence:
`chosen.pop("error", None)
 decided.update(chosen=chosen, start=True)
 return json.dumps(dict(chosen, started=time.time()))` vs `decided.update(chosen=chosen, start=True)
 return json.dumps(dict(chosen, started=time.time()))`

finding: Placement (module loads, filesystem rules, possible git calls) runs while the marker lock is held, but a waiting caller gives up after 2 s
why: A second parallel refused call that waits longer than LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS gets SafeWriteError instead of the shared move and shows the agent 'could not be created: ... is locked', although the first call is about to record a move.
fix: Resolve the target before taking the lock and re-check it under the lock, or have the loser retry the lock past the first call's placement time.
evidence: h2_move.py:142 `chosen = fresh(root, name, pane, facts, marker)  # placement loads only for a move this call records` inside settle; scripts/safe_write.py:31 `LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS = 2.0` and :143-144 `raise SafeWriteError("is locked", target)`; scripts/placement.py:288,326 `_git_top` / `_git(... timeout=repo_list.GIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS)` (20 s each when a git redirect variable is set); h2_move.py:152-153 returns `failed(name, pane, f"move record: {problem}")`. Failing input: two parallel refused tool calls in one session where placement takes more than 2 s (cold disk, antivirus scan, GIT_DIR set); the test only holds the lock 0.5 s (test_h2_move.py:669).

finding: Possible: a contended marker lock still reaches the agent as 'the session worktree could not be created ... run create-worktree --name', the retry-me-shown-as-failure defect f093 named
why: f093's retry-me message was removed, but settle() holds the lock while it runs placement and the dead-owner check, so a second call that waits past LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS (2 s) gets SafeWriteError, which plan() turns into failed(...), which the guard words as a failed creation and nudges toward a second hand-made worktree.
fix: Return a distinct key (for example retry) for a lock timeout and have h2_hint print 'try the command again' without the create-worktree tail, or keep the lock only around the read and write and run placement outside it.
evidence: h2_move.py:149-153 'except Exception as problem: ... return failed(name, pane, f"move record: {problem}")' with settle() calling fresh()/owner_is_dead() inside update_locked (:131,:142); safe_write.py LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS = 2.0; protected_branch_guard.py:455-458 'the session worktree could not be created: {chosen['error']}. Fix that, or run ... create-worktree --name <name>'.

finding: Possible: the placement and owner checks now run under the marker lock, so a second concurrent call can time out and be reported as a failed creation
why: settle() calls fresh() (placement.target_for runs git with a timeout) and owner_is_dead() while holding the lock, and safe_write gives up after 2 s, so a slow first call makes the second return 'move record: is locked', which h2_hint wraps as 'could not be created ... Fix that, or run create-worktree' (the r-012 retry-me-shown-as-failure shape again).
fix: Keep slow work outside the lock (decide under it, run placement before taking it), or have plan return a distinct retry result that h2_hint renders as 'try the command again'.
evidence: h2_move.py:142 `chosen = fresh(root, name, pane, facts, marker)` inside settle; h2_move.py:152-153 `except Exception as problem: return failed(name, pane, f"move record: {problem}")`; scripts/safe_write.py:31 `LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS = 2.0` and :144 `raise SafeWriteError("is locked", target)`; hooks/lib/protected_branch_guard.py:455-458 `the session worktree could not be created: {chosen['error']}. Fix that, or run ...`. Inferred from reading; not run.

finding: An exception raised by create() records no outcome, so the marker keeps promising a worktree nothing is making
why: run() calls create() unguarded; a raise (subprocess.TimeoutExpired after 900 s, or OSError from a missing cwd or shell) skips record(), so the guard reports 'being created' until RETRY_AFTER and the module docstring's `created`/`error` outcome contract is broken.
fix: Wrap create(args) in try/except Exception and record(args.marker, error=<exception text>) before re-raising or returning 1.
evidence: afk-move.py:266-268 `path, error = create(args)` / `record(args.marker, **({"created": str(path)} if path is not None else {"error": error}))` with create() at :109-111 `subprocess.run([...], cwd=args.cwd or args.repo, env=env, timeout=900)`; docstring :16-17 'The outcome goes into --marker: `created` or `error`'. Failing input: --cwd names a directory removed after the refusal (FileNotFoundError), or create-worktree runs past 900 s.

finding: Possible double-duty field: the placement answer's `folder` slot (P_FOLDER) means the main checkout, the root/short-name folder, or the derived sibling base depending on mode
why: Parent mode returns `main` in the folder slot with rule `main`, yet the same slot is the worktree parent for `inside` and `dir` answers, so each use of `$P_FOLDER` (lines 382-385, 392, 396, 402) needs the mode in mind to read right.
fix: Give the refused-main answer its own field or message text (or name the slot generically, e.g. `anchor`) and document per state what it holds.
evidence: `return "refused", target, main, "main", ""` ... `refuse_exit "parent $WORKTREE_PARENT is inside the main checkout $P_FOLDER ..."` vs `WORKTREE_PARENT="$P_FOLDER"` (inside / dir branches)

finding: Marker readers were not updated for the new lock sibling: drop_markers unlinks the .move file but leaves its `.<name>.afk.lock`
why: Every marker now gets a permanent `.<key>.move.afk.lock` beside it (safe_write never deletes lock files, safe_write.py:135) and neither remove-worktree's drop_markers nor worktree-prune cleans them, so afk-session accumulates one lock file per session.
fix: Have drop_markers also unlink the marker's `.{name}.afk.lock` sibling (the `*.move` glob at remove-worktree.py:253 correctly ignores it), or note the leak as accepted in D-64.
evidence: remove-worktree.py:263-264 `if same(target, path): marker.unlink(missing_ok=True)`; safe_write.py:135 `# Never delete the lock file`; hooks/worktree-prune.sh:11 deletes only `*.fallback`; the tests filter it out with `_left_in(...) - {f".{marker.name}.afk.lock"}` (test_h2_move.py:683).

finding: Two-calls-at-once tests lean on real sleeps inside the safe writer's 2.0 s lock-wait budget
why: the lock holder also loads placement.py (and, in the dead-session test, probes the process) under the lock; on a slow machine the second thread can exceed LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS and return a 'move record: ... is locked' failure, so a loaded CI host fails a correct implementation.
fix: Hold the lock with a threading.Event handshake (second thread starts only after the first is inside the lock) instead of a fixed sleep, or assert on the lock-timeout error separately.
evidence: line 669 `lambda *a: (time.sleep(0.5), real_fresh(*a))[1]`; line 699 `time.sleep(0.3)`; scripts/safe_write.py:34 `LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS = 2.0`; failed() results carry a distinct `name`, so the `len(names) == 1` assert would fail

finding: The second call in the spawn-failure test cannot tell 'read the recorded error' from 'tried to spawn again'
why: The stubbed spawn raises the same OSError message every time, so a second call that wrongly re-spawned would return an identical error string and the test would pass; there is no spawn-count assertion.
fix: Count spawn calls in the stub and assert exactly one after the second plan().
evidence: test_h2_move.py:796-806 `def broken(argv, env): raise OSError("no such interpreter")` ... `again = module.plan(...)` / `assert again["error"] == chosen["error"]`
